nodes.key_innovation: Introduce a gating module between down-projection and up-projection matrices in LoRA, optimized using proximal gradient method with L1 regularization to dynamically control rank sparsity during training. After training, zeroed ranks are pruned to obtain a compact rank-optimal LoRA module.

Parameterizes incremental updates as PΛQ (SVD form) and adaptively allocates parameter budget by pruning singular values based on importance scores that combine sensitivity and uncertainty, allowing critical weight matrices to have higher ranks

S-LoRA separates batched base model computation from on-the-fly LoRA computation (xAB), uses Unified Paging with a unified memory pool to manage dynamic adapter weights and KV cache tensors, employs custom CUDA kernels for heterogeneous batching of LoRA computation with varying ranks and sequence lengths, and implements a novel tensor parallelism strategy that minimizes communication overhead for added LoRA computation by scheduling communications on small intermediate tensors and fusing them with base model communications.

Treats LoRA modules as Mixture of Experts and uses a gating network with Top-k routing for dynamic combination. Introduces contrastive learning among experts to mitigate random routing, treating outputs of the same expert as positives and different experts as negatives.

Treat each layer of trained LoRAs as a distinct expert and implement hierarchical weight control by integrating learnable gating functions within each layer to learn optimal composition weights, enhanced with a gating balancing loss to maintain uniform weight distribution

Plugin-based MoE architecture combining multiple LoRA adapters as experts with a router mechanism, featuring localized balancing constraints that split experts into two groups - one for downstream task learning and another for aligning world knowledge with human instructions, enabling coordinated expert utilization without disrupting stored knowledge.

edges.description: AdaLoRA builds upon SoRA's SVD-based low-rank adaptation approach (PΛQ parameterization) and improves efficiency by introducing adaptive budget allocation that prunes singular values based on importance scores combining sensitivity and uncertainty, rather than relying on regularization-based sparsity like SoRA.

S-LoRA extends the LoRA paradigm by enabling efficient serving of thousands of concurrent LoRA adapters. While LoRA provides parameter-efficient fine-tuning, S-LoRA focuses on the systems-level challenge of serving multiple adapters simultaneously with optimized batching, memory management, and tensor parallelism.

MoELoRA extends LoRA by treating LoRA modules as Mixture of Experts, introducing a gating network with Top-k routing for dynamic expert combination and contrastive learning to mitigate random routing issues.
MoELoRA shares similar sparse gating concepts with SoRA but applies them to expert routing in a MoE framework. Both aim for efficient parameter utilization through dynamic selection mechanisms.

Both methods use adaptive mechanisms - AdaLoRA for rank allocation and MoELoRA for expert routing. MoELoRA extends this adaptive concept to a mixture-of-experts architecture with contrastive learning guidance.
Both methods deal with managing multiple LoRA adapters/experts. S-LoRA focuses on serving multiple adapters efficiently, while MoELoRA dynamically combines multiple LoRA experts through routing.

MOLE inherits the Mixture of Experts paradigm from MoELoRA for LoRA adaptation but introduces hierarchical weight control with learnable gating functions within each layer. MOLE differs in its approach to expert composition, using layer-wise gating mechanisms and a balancing loss to maintain uniform weight distribution, potentially improving upon MoELoRA's expert selection strategy.

LoRAMoE extends MoELoRA by introducing localized balancing constraints and a dual-group expert architecture that separates downstream task learning from world knowledge alignment, enabling more coordinated expert utilization without disrupting stored knowledge.

LoRAMoE builds upon LoRA by utilizing multiple LoRA adapters as experts within a Mixture of Experts framework, transforming single adapter adaptation into a scalable plugin-based architecture with intelligent routing.

LoRAMoE shares the conceptual foundation of MOLE (Mixture of LoRA Experts) by combining multiple LoRA adapters through an expert routing mechanism, but LoRAMoE enhances this with localized balancing constraints and specialized expert groups.
